successors.note: The Stairs expedition ended the kingdom by killing Msiri on 20 December 1891 and installed Mukanda-Bantu over 'a radius of only 20 km from Bunkeya'; the chieftainship 'continues to this day under the title Mwata Msiri'. The Msiri page: the Compagnie du Katanga administered the territory; Britain accepted the Free State's possession (Anglo-Belgian agreement 1894). [Fix af-06, 2026-10-19: the land is the redrawn Yeke shape, no longer all of Katanga (which held the whole Luba region, 909 cells, and 443 cells of the Lunda shape); congo-free-state still gains the whole of Katanga from the Yeke in its ledger 4, a superset that also holds Luba land it gains separately in 1889 (that dossier is outside this pass).]

correction.text: Msiri's state as the Bunkeya page bounds it, 'from the Luapula River south to the Congo-Zambezi watershed' and 'from Lake Mweru in the east to the Lualaba River in the west': the part of Katanga east of the Lualaba (25 E) and south of the Luba region

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: from 1867 Msiri held the west bank of the Luapula (Msiri page); the Bunkeya page bounds his state 'from the Luapula River south to the Congo-Zambezi watershed' and 'from Lake Mweru in the east to the Lualaba River in the west'; the Yeke page says it 'stopped the southwards expansion of the Luba Empire' and the Msiri page puts the Luba to Msiri's north-west. The block is Katanga within 25-31.5 E, 14-8.4 S, less the Luba region (340 cells, about 86,000 km2). Area check: the Yeke page gives 'about half a million square kilometres' with no year (the Yeke infobox gives no area and its map caption is c. 1880); the shape is 0.17 of that figure, beyond a factor of two. Decision: the shape stands, because the two boundary sentences describe a block of this size and the half-million figure can only count the tributary and trade sphere (the page says Msiri ruled through 'alliances through marriage' and force of arms and does not separate tributaries from ruled land). Boundaries are approximate: the Lualaba edge is the 25 E meridian, the north edge the Luba region's own southern edge. [Fix af-06, 2026-10-19: BLOCKING shape: the old shape was all of Katanga (1,628 cells), which contained the whole of luba-empire's 1700-1889 shape (909 cells, with the capital Mwibele at 26.4 E, 8.63 S) and 443 cells of kingdom-of-lunda's 1856-1887 shape, so three states held the same land 1867-1887. The reviewer proposed Katanga minus the Luba region; this block also leaves out the 379 cells of Katanga-minus-Luba that lie west of 25 E (the Lunda side) or north of 8.4 S (the Tanganyika shore), which no page gives to Msiri and which cleared the Lunda disc completely. The Bunkeya boundary sentences would also take the Luba region's southern strip (10 S to Lake Mweru); luba-empire draws that as Luba's and is outside this pass.]

region.text: Bunkeya and its district, the first chieftainship: 150 km around Bunkeya without the Luba region and without Kazembe's Luapula-Mweru shape

ledger.note: 1856: Msiri's chieftainship begins at Bunkeya. 'existing from about 1856 to 1891 under one king, Msiri'; infobox: Msiri's rise to power 1856. He 'got himself appointed as successor to a Wasanga chief west of the Luapula River' (no year). The Kazembe page: in 1856 Msiri travelled through Kazembe and asked permission of King Chinyanta Munona. [Fix af-06, 2026-10-19: counterpart changed from kingdom-of-kazembe to nobody: the disc is cut by Kazembe's shape and the Wasanga chiefdom Msiri took over was not a state with a dossier; the west bank passes from Kazembe only in 1867 (next event). Region cut by the Luba region and Kazembe's 1740 shape.]

region.text: 'most of the Mwata's territory and trade on the west bank of the Luapula River' (the Luapula valley and the DRC shore of Lake Mweru, without the Luba region)

ledger.note: 1867: Msiri takes the west bank of the Luapula. 'By 1867, he had taken control of most of the Mwata's territory and trade on the west bank of the Luapula River.' [Fix af-06, 2026-10-19: region = the Kazembe shape on the Congo side minus the Luba region (46 of its 200 cells lay in the Luba region); all of it lies inside the new 1867 shape.]

region.text: the rest of Msiri's state: the Katanga block east of the Lualaba and south of the Luba region, less the Luapula west bank gained in 1867

ledger.note: 1870 (bridge): Msiri conquers the neighbouring peoples. 'Once installed he conquered the neighbouring tribes and expanded the chieftainship into a kingdom'; it 'stopped the southwards expansion of the Luba Empire' and 'subjugated tribes in the southwest, on the trading route to Angola' (Yeke page). The pages give no years for these conquests (the Garanganze and Msiri pages, re-read in the fix pass, date only 1867 and 1870 for Kazembe, and the Msiri page has the Wasanga chieftainships overthrown about 30 years before 1891, c. 1861); 1870 is the year Msiri and Tippu Tip are said to have killed a Mwata Kazembe (Msiri page). Confidence 1: a bridge, and the drawn land is a proxy. [Fix af-06, 2026-10-19: the old region was all of Katanga from 'nobody', which was Luba land (luba-empire 1700-1889) and partly Lunda's. The redrawn block excludes the Luba region and the Lunda shape, so no drawn Luba or Lunda land is taken and no loss is owed by luba-empire or kingdom-of-lunda; the reviewer's counterparts apply only to land the shape still held, none, so 'nobody' (the Sanga, Lamba and other peoples with no dossier) stands.]

ledger.note: 1891 December: Msiri is killed and the Yeke kingdom ends. 'On December 14, 1891 the armed Stairs Expedition of the CFS arrived in Bunkeya with 400 troops and porters'; Msiri died on 20 December 1891 (Yeke infobox) when Bodson shot him (Msiri page); 'The scramble for Katanga was won by Leopold's Stairs Expedition, which ended the kingdom by killing Msiri' (Yeke page). Stairs installed Mukanda-Bantu over a 20 km radius. [Fix af-06, 2026-10-19: region = the redrawn shape.]

wars.outcome: The Free State's Stairs Expedition reached Bunkeya on 14 December 1891 (Msiri page) and Msiri was killed on 20 December (Yeke infobox); the kingdom ended and was taken over for the Congo Free State.
wars.note: Cecil Rhodes's BSAC also sent expeditions (Yeke page); the British accepted the Free State's possession of Katanga in the Anglo-Belgian agreement of 1894.

certainty.note: A trading kingdom with no frontier given; the Bunkeya page names the Luapula and Lake Mweru (east), the Lualaba (west) and the Congo-Zambezi watershed (south), the area figure of half a million km2 has no year.

notes: Cliopatria has no Yeke kingdom. The pages give 'about half a million square kilometres' without a year and no boundary; Katanga province (the gazetteer's Katanga admin1, confidence 3) stands in from 1867 and a 150 km disc around Bunkeya before. The pages do not date the conquest of the Lamba, Sanga or Lunda areas or of the Luba south-east. Msiri's death date is 20 December 1891 in the Msiri page (the Bunkeya page says only 1891). Not settled: the Silva Porto and Bié connection, the Katanga Company (1891) and the Bia expedition (not on the pages). Page budget (2-5): four pages. [Fix af-06, 2026-10-19: (1) BLOCKING shape: Katanga province (1,628 cells) is replaced by the Katanga block east of 25 E, between 14 S and 8.4 S, less the Luba region (340 cells), from the Bunkeya page's own boundaries (Luapula and Lake Mweru east, Lualaba west, Congo-Zambezi watershed south); the first chieftainship (1856-1866) is cut by the Luba region and Kazembe's 1740 shape; the shape no longer overlaps luba-empire (0 cells), kingdom-of-lunda's 309 km disc (0) or kingdom-of-kazembe from 1867 (0). The page's half million km2 is 6 times the block; judged to count the tribute sphere (keyframe note). (2) The 1870 gain stays 'nobody' at confidence 1: no drawn Luba or Lunda land is taken any more. The pages date no conquest besides 1867 and 1870 (Garanganze, Msiri and Bunkeya re-read); the Msiri page implies c. 1861 for the overthrow of the Wasanga chieftainships. (3) Not touched here, for the Free State's dossier: congo-free-state ledger 4 gains the whole of Katanga from yeke-kingdom in 1891-12 and its keyframe 0 subtracts all of Katanga, a superset of this shape that also holds the Luba region it gains separately in 1889.]
